summary.text: A beach is a landform of loose particles, such as sand, pebbles or shell pieces, lying beside a body of water.
Most beaches are on coasts, where waves and currents drop sediment and keep reworking it.
In temperate areas a beach's shape shifts with the seasons: calm summer waves push sand up and build it higher, while stormy winter waves strip it away and lower it.

facts.label: Share of coastlines
facts.value: Sandy beaches cover about one third

facts.label: Possible loss by 2100
facts.value: Up to 50 percent of sandy beaches

facts.label: Beach berm
facts.value: The active shoreline deposit, with crest and face

facts.label: Where sand comes from
facts.value: Eroded offshore rocks, headlands and scree

items.prompt: You visit the same temperate beach in midsummer and again after a stormy winter. What change are you most likely to see?

options.label: The beach sits higher after winter
The beach sits lower after winter
The beach looks exactly the same
The beach has turned into a dune

items.explain: Stronger, more frequent winter waves pull sediment off the berm and dune, so the beach profile is lower in the storm season.

items.prompt: Behind a beach, past where even storm waves reach, the sand piles into mounds. What is shaping them?

options.label: Tides rising higher each day
Currents running along the shore
Wind moving the grains inland
Rivers dropping mud at the coast

items.explain: Beyond the reach of waves, wind shapes sand-sized grains, and where wind spreads grains inland the deposit becomes a dune.

items.prompt: On calm summer days, which way do gentle waves tend to carry sand on a temperate beach?

options.label: Up the beach toward the berm
Out to sea into deep water
Straight down into the seabed
Nowhere, since calm waves move nothing

items.explain: Gentle summer waves move sediment up the beach toward the berm, where it is left behind as the water recedes.

items.prompt: Some forecasts warn about sandy beaches by the year 2100. How large a share could disappear?

options.label: About 5 percent
About 15 percent
About 25 percent
As much as 50 percent

items.explain: Some estimates say as much as half of Earth's sandy beaches could disappear by 2100 because of sea level rise driven by climate change.

items.prompt: Why are dunes behind a beach worth protecting for the people and wildlife living farther inland?

options.label: They stop the tide from rising
They shield inland areas from extreme weather
They make the sea water less salty
They hold back all river flooding

items.explain: Preserved beaches and their dunes protect inland ecosystems and human infrastructure from extreme weather.

items.prompt: A storm strikes at the same time as an unusually high tide. What can happen to the land behind the beach?

options.label: It gains a thick new layer of sand
It stays untouched behind the berm
It turns into a coral reef
Large amounts of it can be washed away

items.explain: When storms coincide with unusually high tides, receding water may erode substantial material from the coastal plain or dunes behind the berm.
